targets.exact_proposed_header:
theorem shifted_absolute_convex_differentiable_iff (c : ℝ) :
    ConvexOn ℝ Set.univ (fun x : ℝ => |x - c|) ∧
      ∀ x : ℝ, DifferentiableAt ℝ (fun w : ℝ => |w - c|) x ↔ x ≠ c

theorem hinge_convex_differentiable_iff {E : Type*} [NormedAddCommGroup E]
    [InnerProductSpace ℝ E] [FiniteDimensional ℝ E] (a : E) :
    ConvexOn ℝ Set.univ (fun x : E => max (1 - inner ℝ a x) 0) ∧
      ∀ x : E, DifferentiableAt ℝ (fun w : E => max (1 - inner ℝ a w) 0) x ↔
        inner ℝ a x ≠ 1

theorem labelled_hinge_convex_differentiable_iff {E : Type*} [NormedAddCommGroup E]
    [InnerProductSpace ℝ E] [FiniteDimensional ℝ E] (y : ℝ) (z : E) :
    ConvexOn ℝ Set.univ (fun x : E => max (1 - y * inner ℝ z x) 0) ∧
      (∀ x : E, DifferentiableAt ℝ (fun w : E => max (1 - y * inner ℝ z w) 0) x ↔
        y * inner ℝ z x ≠ 1) ∧
      (Differentiable ℝ (fun w : E => max (1 - y * inner ℝ z w) 0) ↔ y • z = 0)

proposed_source_repair.original_ambiguity: Unqualified hinge is not differentiable could be read as every point or every label/feature, both false. Labels/features are unconstrained in the displayed paragraph.
proposed_source_repair.explicit_proposal: At each point, the hinge is differentiable iff its affine margin is not exactly zero. It is globally differentiable iff y•z=0; otherwise a genuine boundary kink exists. This is an explicit qualification, not author-endorsed erratum.
proposed_source_repair.simple_counterexample: y=0 or z=0 gives constant max(1,0)=1, differentiable everywhere.
